research.name: Zhejiang University, in collaboration with Dr. Jianghao Liu, Paris Brain Institute (ICM)
highlights: Research content: using signal detection theory to study how imagination affects perception.

Design and methods: the protocol pairs a near-threshold perceptual detection task with an imagery task, plus electrophysiological and neuromodulation measures of visual-cortical and prefrontal involvement.

Role: project lead, with Dr. Jianghao Liu as collaborator; built the experimental platform at Zhejiang University and was responsible for participant recruitment, data collection and analysis, and quality control.
Imaging studies are in preparation: a simultaneous fMRI–EEG study of where and when imagery enters perception, and a TMS–EEG study of whether the visual-cortical node is necessary.

research.name: Zhejiang University
research.position: Acquired Silent Reading Disorder: A Single-Case Study
highlights: A single-case study I designed and led independently.

Case: a participant who lost spontaneous inner speech after practising speed reading — deliberate suppression of inner pronunciation combined with forced acceleration — and could no longer read silently without external support.

Experiment: a picture–text matching task over one to ten characters, run under five pacing conditions (no aid, and auditory rhythms at 4, 2, 1 and 0.5 Hz), to test whether an external rhythm restores silent reading.
Hypothesis: inner speech fails to reach conscious access, putatively because the left SMA is suppressed by over-activity of the right SMA, which would impair the efference copy.
Treatment and outcome: low-frequency TMS over the right SMA; the participant recovered, consistent with the hypothesis.
